NKJV.1: Now these are the nations which the LORD left, that He might test Israel by them, that is, all who had not known any of the wars in Canaan
NKJV.2: (this was only so that the generations of the children of Israel might be taught to know war, at least those who had not formerly known it),
NKJV.3: namely, five lords of the Philistines, all the Canaanites, the Sidonians, and the Hivites who dwelt in Mount Lebanon, from Mount Baal Hermon to the entrance of Hamath.
NKJV.4: And they were left, that He might test Israel by them, to know whether they would obey the commandments of the LORD, which He had commanded their fathers by the hand of Moses.
NKJV.5: Thus the children of Israel dwelt among the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites.
NKJV.6: And they took their daughters to be their wives, and gave their daughters to their sons; and they served their gods.
NKJV.7: So the children of Israel did evil in the sight of the LORD. They forgot the LORD their God, and served the Baals and Asherahs.
NKJV.8: Therefore the anger of the LORD was hot against Israel, and He sold them into the hand of Cushan-Rishathaim king of Mesopotamia; and the children of Israel served Cushan-Rishathaim eight years.
NKJV.9: When the children of Israel cried out to the LORD, the LORD raised up a deliverer for the children of Israel, who delivered them: Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb’s younger brother.
NKJV.10: The Spirit of the LORD came upon him, and he judged Israel. He went out to war, and the LORD delivered Cushan-Rishathaim king of Mesopotamia into his hand; and his hand prevailed over Cushan-Rishathaim.
NKJV.11: So the land had rest for forty years. Then Othniel the son of Kenaz died.
NKJV.12: And the children of Israel again did evil in the sight of the LORD. So the LORD strengthened Eglon king of Moab against Israel, because they had done evil in the sight of the LORD.
NKJV.13: Then he gathered to himself the people of Ammon and Amalek, went and defeated Israel, and took possession of the City of Palms.
NKJV.14: So the children of Israel served Eglon king of Moab eighteen years.
NKJV.15: But when the children of Israel cried out to the LORD, the LORD raised up a deliverer for them: Ehud the son of Gera, the Benjamite, a left-handed man. By him the children of Israel sent tribute to Eglon king of Moab.
NKJV.16: Now Ehud made himself a dagger (it was double-edged and a cubit in length) and fastened it under his clothes on his right thigh.
NKJV.17: So he brought the tribute to Eglon king of Moab. (Now Eglon was a very fat man.)
NKJV.18: And when he had finished presenting the tribute, he sent away the people who had carried the tribute.
NKJV.19: But he himself turned back from the stone images that were at Gilgal, and said, “I have a secret message for you, O king.” He said, “Keep silence!” And all who attended him went out from him.
NKJV.20: So Ehud came to him (now he was sitting upstairs in his cool private chamber). Then Ehud said, “I have a message from God for you.” So he arose from his seat.
NKJV.21: Then Ehud reached with his left hand, took the dagger from his right thigh, and thrust it into his belly.
NKJV.22: Even the hilt went in after the blade, and the fat closed over the blade, for he did not draw the dagger out of his belly; and his entrails came out.
NKJV.23: Then Ehud went out through the porch and shut the doors of the upper room behind him and locked them.
NKJV.24: When he had gone out, Eglon’s servants came to look, and to their surprise, the doors of the upper room were locked. So they said, “He is probably attending to his needs in the cool chamber.”
NKJV.25: So they waited till they were embarrassed, and still he had not opened the doors of the upper room. Therefore they took the key and opened them. And there was their master, fallen dead on the floor.
NKJV.26: But Ehud had escaped while they delayed, and passed beyond the stone images and escaped to Seirah.
NKJV.27: And it happened, when he arrived, that he blew the trumpet in the mountains of Ephraim, and the children of Israel went down with him from the mountains; and he led them.
NKJV.28: Then he said to them, “Follow me, for the LORD has delivered your enemies the Moabites into your hand.” So they went down after him, seized the fords of the Jordan leading to Moab, and did not allow anyone to cross over.
NKJV.29: And at that time they killed about ten thousand men of Moab, all stout men of valor; not a man escaped.
NKJV.30: So Moab was subdued that day under the hand of Israel. And the land had rest for eighty years.
NKJV.31: After him was Shamgar the son of Anath, who killed six hundred men of the Philistines with an ox goad; and he also delivered Israel.

NASB.1: Now these are the nations which the LORD left, to test Israel by them ([that is], all who had not experienced any of the wars of Canaan;
NASB.2: only in order that the generations of the sons of Israel might be taught war, those who had not experienced it formerly).
NASB.3: [These nations are]: the five lords of the Philistines and all the Canaanites and the Sidonians and the Hivites who lived in Mount Lebanon, from Mount Baal-hermon as far as Lebo-hamath.
NASB.4: They were for testing Israel, to find out if they would obey the commandments of the LORD, which He had commanded their fathers through Moses.
NASB.5: The sons of Israel lived among the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites;
NASB.6: and they took their daughters for themselves as wives, and gave their own daughters to their sons, and served their gods.
NASB.7: The sons of Israel did what was evil in the sight of the LORD, and forgot the LORD their God and served the Baals and the Asheroth.
NASB.8: Then the anger of the LORD was kindled against Israel, so that He sold them into the hands of Cushan-rishathaim king of Mesopotamia; and the sons of Israel served Cushan-rishathaim eight years.
NASB.9: When the sons of Israel cried to the LORD, the LORD raised up a deliverer for the sons of Israel to deliver them, Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother.
NASB.10: The Spirit of the LORD came upon him, and he judged Israel. When he went out to war, the LORD gave Cushan-rishathaim king of Mesopotamia into his hand, so that he prevailed over Cushan-rishathaim.
NASB.11: Then the land had rest forty years. And Othniel the son of Kenaz died.
NASB.12: Now the sons of Israel again did evil in the sight of the LORD. So the LORD strengthened Eglon the king of Moab against Israel, because they had done evil in the sight of the LORD.
NASB.13: And he gathered to himself the sons of Ammon and Amalek; and he went and defeated Israel, and they possessed the city of the palm trees.
NASB.14: The sons of Israel served Eglon the king of Moab eighteen years.
NASB.15: But when the sons of Israel cried to the LORD, the LORD raised up a deliverer for them, Ehud the son of Gera, the Benjamite, a left-handed man. And the sons of Israel sent tribute by him to Eglon the king of Moab.
NASB.16: Ehud made himself a sword which had two edges, a cubit in length, and he bound it on his right thigh under his cloak.
NASB.17: He presented the tribute to Eglon king of Moab. Now Eglon was a very fat man.
NASB.18: It came about when he had finished presenting the tribute, that he sent away the people who had carried the tribute.
NASB.19: But he himself turned back from the idols which were at Gilgal, and said, 'I have a secret message for you, O king.' And he said, 'Keep silence.' And all who attended him left him.
NASB.20: Ehud came to him while he was sitting alone in his cool roof chamber. And Ehud said, 'I have a message from God for you.' And he arose from his seat.
NASB.21: Ehud stretched out his left hand, took the sword from his right thigh and thrust it into his belly.
NASB.22: The handle also went in after the blade, and the fat closed over the blade, for he did not draw the sword out of his belly; and the refuse came out.
NASB.23: Then Ehud went out into the vestibule and shut the doors of the roof chamber behind him, and locked [them].
NASB.24: When he had gone out, his servants came and looked, and behold, the doors of the roof chamber were locked; and they said, 'He is only relieving himself in the cool room.'
NASB.25: They waited until they became anxious; but behold, he did not open the doors of the roof chamber. Therefore they took the key and opened them, and behold, their master had fallen to the floor dead.
NASB.26: Now Ehud escaped while they were delaying, and he passed by the idols and escaped to Seirah.
NASB.27: It came about when he had arrived, that he blew the trumpet in the hill country of Ephraim; and the sons of Israel went down with him from the hill country, and he [was] in front of them.
NASB.28: He said to them, 'Pursue [them], for the LORD has given your enemies the Moabites into your hands.' So they went down after him and seized the fords of the Jordan opposite Moab, and did not allow anyone to cross.
NASB.29: They struck down at that time about ten thousand Moabites, all robust and valiant men; and no one escaped.
NASB.30: So Moab was subdued that day under the hand of Israel. And the land was undisturbed for eighty years.
NASB.31: After him came Shamgar the son of Anath, who struck down six hundred Philistines with an oxgoad; and he also saved Israel.

WEB.1: Now these are the nations which Yahweh left, to test Israel by them, even as many as had not known all the wars of Canaan;
WEB.2: only that the generations of the children of Israel might know, to teach them war, at least those who knew nothing of it before:
WEB.3: the five lords of the Philistines, all the Canaanites, the Sidonians, and the Hivites who lived on Mount Lebanon, from Mount Baal Hermon to the entrance of Hamath.
WEB.4: They were left to test Israel by them, to know whether they would listen to Yahweh’s commandments, which he commanded their fathers by Moses.
WEB.5: The children of Israel lived among the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites.
WEB.6: They took their daughters to be their wives, and gave their own daughters to their sons and served their gods.
WEB.7: The children of Israel did that which was evil in Yahweh’s sight, and forgot Yahweh their God, and served the Baals and the Asheroth.
WEB.8: Therefore Yahweh’s anger burned against Israel, and he sold them into the hand of Cushan Rishathaim king of Mesopotamia; and the children of Israel served Cushan Rishathaim eight years.
WEB.9: When the children of Israel cried to Yahweh, Yahweh raised up a savior to the children of Israel, who saved them, even Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb’s younger brother.
WEB.10: Yahweh’s Spirit came on him, and he judged Israel; and he went out to war, and Yahweh delivered Cushan Rishathaim king of Mesopotamia into his hand. His hand prevailed against Cushan Rishathaim.
WEB.11: The land had rest forty years, then Othniel the son of Kenaz died.
WEB.12: The children of Israel again did that which was evil in Yahweh’s sight, and Yahweh strengthened Eglon the king of Moab against Israel, because they had done that which was evil in Yahweh’s sight.
WEB.13: He gathered the children of Ammon and Amalek to himself; and he went and struck Israel, and they possessed the city of palm trees.
WEB.14: The children of Israel served Eglon the king of Moab eighteen years.
WEB.15: But when the children of Israel cried to Yahweh, Yahweh raised up a savior for them, Ehud the son of Gera, the Benjamite, a left-handed man. The children of Israel sent tribute by him to Eglon the king of Moab.
WEB.16: Ehud made himself a sword which had two edges, a cubit  in length; and he wore it under his clothing on his right thigh.
WEB.17: He offered the tribute to Eglon king of Moab. Now Eglon was a very fat man.
WEB.18: When he had finished offering the tribute, he sent away the people who carried the tribute.
WEB.19: But he himself turned back from the stone idols that were by Gilgal, and said, “I have a secret message for you, O king.” The king said, “Keep silence!” All who stood by him left him.
WEB.20: Ehud came to him; and he was sitting by himself alone in the cool upper room. Ehud said, “I have a message from God to you.” He arose out of his seat.
WEB.21: Ehud put out his left hand, and took the sword from his right thigh, and thrust it into his body:
WEB.22: and the handle also went in after the blade; and the fat closed on the blade, for he didn’t draw the sword out of his body; and it came out behind.
WEB.23: Then Ehud went out onto the porch, and shut the doors of the upper room on him, and locked them.
WEB.24: After he had gone, his servants came and saw that the doors of the upper room were locked. They said, “Surely he is covering his feet  in the upper room.”
WEB.25: They waited until they were ashamed; and behold, he didn’t open the doors of the upper room. Therefore they took the key and opened them, and behold, their lord had fallen down dead on the floor.
WEB.26: Ehud escaped while they waited, passed beyond the stone idols, and escaped to Seirah.
WEB.27: When he had come, he blew a trumpet in the hill country of Ephraim; and the children of Israel went down with him from the hill country, and he led them.
WEB.28: He said to them, “Follow me; for Yahweh has delivered your enemies the Moabites into your hand.” They followed him, and took the fords of the Jordan against the Moabites, and didn’t allow any man to pass over.
WEB.29: They struck at that time about ten thousand men of Moab, every strong man, and every man of valor. No man escaped.
WEB.30: So Moab was subdued that day under the hand of Israel. Then the land had rest eighty years.
WEB.31: After him was Shamgar the son of Anath, who struck six hundred men of the Philistines with an ox goad. He also saved Israel.

CSB17.1: These are the nations the LORD left in order to test all those in Israel who had experienced <sup>[1]</sup> none of the wars in Canaan. <sup>ⓒ</sup>
CSB17.2: This was to teach the future generations of the Israelites how to fight in battle, especially those who had not fought before. <sup>[2]</sup>
CSB17.3: These nations included the five rulers <sup>ⓓ</sup> of the Philistines <sup>ⓔ</sup> and all of the Canaanites, the Sidonians, <sup>ⓕ</sup> and the Hivites <sup>ⓖ</sup> who lived in the Lebanese mountains from Mount Baal-hermon as far as the entrance to Hamath. <sup>[3]</sup>
CSB17.4: The LORD left them to test Israel, to determine if they would keep the LORD’s commands he had given their fathers through <sup>[4]</sup> Moses. <sup>ⓗ</sup>
CSB17.5: But they settled among the Canaanites, Hethites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
CSB17.6: The Israelites took their daughters as wives for themselves, gave their own daughters to their sons, and worshiped their gods. <sup>ⓘ</sup>
CSB17.7: The Israelites did what was evil in the LORD’s sight; they forgot the LORD their God <sup>ⓙ</sup> and worshiped the Baals and the Asherahs.
CSB17.8: The LORD’s anger burned against Israel, and he sold them to <sup>[5]</sup> King Cushan-rishathaim <sup>[6]</sup> of Aram-naharaim, <sup>[7]</sup> <sup>ⓚ</sup> and the Israelites served him eight years.
CSB17.9: The Israelites cried out to the LORD. <sup>ⓛ</sup> So the LORD raised up Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb’s youngest brother, <sup>ⓜ</sup> as a deliverer <sup>ⓝ</sup> to save the Israelites.
CSB17.10: The Spirit of the LORD came on him, and he judged Israel. Othniel went out to battle, and the LORD handed over King Cushan-rishathaim of Aram to him, so that Othniel overpowered him.
CSB17.11: Then the land had peace for <sup>ⓐ</sup> forty years, and Othniel son of Kenaz died.
CSB17.12: The Israelites again did what was evil in the LORD’s sight. He gave King Eglon of Moab <sup>ⓑ</sup> power over Israel, because they had done what was evil in the LORD’s sight.
CSB17.13: After Eglon convinced the Ammonites and the Amalekites to join forces with him, he attacked and defeated Israel and took possession of the City of Palms. <sup>[8]</sup> <sup>ⓒ</sup>
CSB17.14: The Israelites served King Eglon of Moab eighteen years.
CSB17.15: Then the Israelites cried out to the LORD, and he raised up Ehud son of Gera, a left-handed <sup>ⓓ</sup> Benjaminite, <sup>[9]</sup> as a deliverer for them. The Israelites sent him with the tribute <sup>ⓔ</sup> for King Eglon of Moab.
CSB17.16: Ehud made himself a double-edged sword eighteen inches long. <sup>[10]</sup> He strapped it to his right thigh under his clothes
CSB17.17: and brought the tribute to King Eglon of Moab, who was an extremely fat man.
CSB17.18: When Ehud had finished presenting the tribute, he dismissed the people who had carried it.
CSB17.19: At the carved images near Gilgal he returned and said, “King Eglon, I have a secret message for you.” The king said, “Silence!” and all his attendants left him.
CSB17.20: Then Ehud approached him while he was sitting alone in his upstairs room where it was cool. Ehud said, “I have a message from God for you,” and the king stood up from his throne.
CSB17.21: Ehud reached with his left hand, took the sword from his right thigh, and plunged it into Eglon’s belly.
CSB17.22: Even the handle went in after the blade, and Eglon’s fat closed in over it, so that Ehud did not withdraw the sword from his belly. And the waste came out. <sup>[11]</sup>
CSB17.23: Ehud escaped by way of the porch, closing and locking the doors of the upstairs room behind him.
CSB17.24: Ehud was gone when Eglon’s servants came in. They looked and found the doors of the upstairs room locked and thought he was relieving himself <sup>[12]</sup> in the cool room.
CSB17.25: The servants waited until they became embarrassed and saw that he had still not opened the doors of the upstairs room. So they took the key and opened the doors — and there was their lord lying dead on the floor!
CSB17.26: Ehud escaped while the servants waited. He passed the Jordan near the carved images and reached Seirah.
CSB17.27: After he arrived, he sounded the ram’s horn throughout the hill country of Ephraim. The Israelites came down with him from the hill country, and he became their leader.
CSB17.28: He told them, “Follow me, because the LORD has handed over your enemies, the Moabites, to you.” So they followed him, captured the fords of the Jordan leading to Moab, and did not allow anyone to cross over. <sup>ⓕ</sup>
CSB17.29: At that time they struck down about ten thousand Moabites, all stout and able-bodied men. Not one of them escaped.
CSB17.30: Moab became subject to Israel that day, and the land had peace for eighty years.
CSB17.31: After Ehud, Shamgar son of Anath became judge. He also delivered Israel, striking down six hundred Philistines with a cattle prod.

AMP.1: Now these are the nations which the LORD left [in order] to test Israel by them (that is, all [the people of Israel] who had not [previously] experienced any of the wars in Canaan;
AMP.2: only in order that the generations of the sons of Israel might be taught war, at least those who had not experienced it previously).
AMP.3: The remaining nations are: the five lords (governors) of the Philistines, all the Canaanites, the Sidonians, and the Hivites who lived on Mount Lebanon from Mount Baal-hermon to the entrance of Hamath.
AMP.4: They were [allowed to remain] for the testing of Israel, to determine whether Israel would listen to and obey the commandments of the LORD, which He had commanded their fathers (ancestors) through Moses.
AMP.5: And the Israelites lived among the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites;
AMP.6: and they took their daughters for themselves as wives and gave their own daughters to their sons, and served their [pagan] gods.
AMP.7: And the Israelites did evil in the sight of the LORD, and they forgot the LORD their God and served the Baals and the Asheroth.
AMP.8: So the anger of the LORD was kindled against Israel, and He sold them into the hand of Cushan-rishathaim king of Mesopotamia; and the Israelites served Cushan-rishathaim eight years.
AMP.9: But when the Israelites cried out to the LORD [for help], the LORD raised up a man to rescue the people of Israel, Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother.
AMP.10: The Spirit of the LORD came upon him, and he judged Israel. He went out to war, and the LORD gave Cushan-rishathaim king of Mesopotamia into his hand, and he prevailed over Cushan-rishathaim.
AMP.11: And the land was at rest [from oppression for] forty years. Then Othniel the son of Kenaz died.
AMP.12: Now the Israelites again did evil in the sight of the LORD, and the LORD strengthened Eglon king of Moab against Israel, since they had done what was evil in the sight of the LORD.
AMP.13: And Eglon gathered to him the sons of Ammon and Amalek, and went and struck down Israel [in defeat], and they took possession of the City of Palm Trees (Jericho).
AMP.14: And the Israelites served Eglon king of Moab eighteen years.
AMP.15: But when the Israelites cried out to the LORD [for help], the LORD raised up a man to rescue them, Ehud the son of Gera, a Benjamite, a left-handed man. And the Israelites sent a gift of tribute by him to Eglon king of Moab.
AMP.16: Now Ehud made for himself a sword a cubit long, which had two edges, and he bound it on his right thigh under his robe.
AMP.17: And he brought the tribute to Eglon king of Moab. Now Eglon was a very fat man.
AMP.18: And when Ehud had finished presenting the tribute, he sent away the people who had carried it.
AMP.19: But Ehud himself turned back from the sculptured stones at Gilgal, [and he returned to Eglon] and said [to him], "I have a secret message for you, O king." Eglon said "Keep silence." And all who attended him left him.
AMP.20: Ehud came to him as he was sitting alone in his [private] cool upper chamber, and Ehud said, "I have a message from God for you." And the king got up from his seat.
AMP.21: Then Ehud reached out with his left hand and took the sword from his right thigh, and plunged it into Eglon's belly.
AMP.22: And the hilt also went in after the blade, and the fat closed over the blade, because Ehud did not draw the sword out of his belly; and the refuse came out.
AMP.23: Then Ehud went out into the vestibule and shut the doors of the upper chamber behind him, and locked them.
AMP.24: When Ehud departed, Eglon's servants came. And when they saw that the doors of the upper room were locked, they said, "He is only relieving himself in the cool room."
AMP.25: They waited [a very long time] until they became embarrassed and uneasy, but he still did not open the doors of the upper room. So [finally] they took the key and opened them, and behold, their master had fallen to the floor, dead.
AMP.26: Now Ehud escaped while they lingered, and he passed beyond the sculptured stones and escaped to Seirah.
AMP.27: When he had arrived, he blew a trumpet in the hill country of Ephraim; and the sons of Israel went down with him from the hill country, and he was in front of them.
AMP.28: And he said to them, "Pursue them, for the LORD has handed over your enemies the Moabites to you." So they went down after him and seized the fords of the Jordan opposite Moab and did not allow anyone to cross.
AMP.29: They struck down at that time about ten thousand Moabite men, all strong, courageous men; not a man escaped.
AMP.30: So Moab was subdued and humbled that day under the hand of Israel, and the land was at rest for eighty years.
AMP.31: After Ehud came Shamgar the son of Anath, who struck down six hundred Philistine men with an oxgoad. He too saved Israel.

NLT.1: These are the nations that the LORD left in the land to test those Israelites who had not experienced the wars of Canaan.
NLT.2: He did this to teach warfare to generations of Israelites who had no experience in battle.
NLT.3: These are the nations: the Philistines (those living under the five Philistine rulers), all the Canaanites, the Sidonians, and the Hivites living in the mountains of Lebanon from Mount Baal-hermon to Lebo-hamath.
NLT.4: These people were left to test the Israelites — to see whether they would obey the commands the LORD had given to their ancestors through Moses.
NLT.5: So the people of Israel lived among the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites,
NLT.6: and they intermarried with them. Israelite sons married their daughters, and Israelite daughters were given in marriage to their sons. And the Israelites served their gods.
NLT.7: The Israelites did evil in the LORD’s sight. They forgot about the LORD their God, and they served the images of Baal and the Asherah poles.
NLT.8: Then the LORD burned with anger against Israel, and he turned them over to King Cushan-rishathaim of Aram-naharaim. And the Israelites served Cushan-rishathaim for eight years.
NLT.9: But when the people of Israel cried out to the LORD for help, the LORD raised up a rescuer to save them. His name was Othniel, the son of Caleb’s younger brother, Kenaz.
NLT.10: The Spirit of the LORD came upon him, and he became Israel’s judge. He went to war against King Cushan-rishathaim of Aram, and the LORD gave Othniel victory over him.
NLT.11: So there was peace in the land for forty years. Then Othniel son of Kenaz died.
NLT.12: Once again the Israelites did evil in the LORD’s sight, and the LORD gave King Eglon of Moab control over Israel because of their evil.
NLT.13: Eglon enlisted the Ammonites and Amalekites as allies, and then he went out and defeated Israel, taking possession of Jericho, the city of palms.
NLT.14: And the Israelites served Eglon of Moab for eighteen years.
NLT.15: But when the people of Israel cried out to the LORD for help, the LORD again raised up a rescuer to save them. His name was Ehud son of Gera, a left-handed man of the tribe of Benjamin. The Israelites sent Ehud to deliver their tribute money to King Eglon of Moab.
NLT.16: So Ehud made a double-edged dagger that was about a foot long, and he strapped it to his right thigh, keeping it hidden under his clothing.
NLT.17: He brought the tribute money to Eglon, who was very fat.
NLT.18: After delivering the payment, Ehud started home with those who had helped carry the tribute.
NLT.19: But when Ehud reached the stone idols near Gilgal, he turned back. He came to Eglon and said, “I have a secret message for you.” So the king commanded his servants, “Be quiet!” and he sent them all out of the room.
NLT.20: Ehud walked over to Eglon, who was sitting alone in a cool upstairs room. And Ehud said, “I have a message from God for you!” As King Eglon rose from his seat,
NLT.21: Ehud reached with his left hand, pulled out the dagger strapped to his right thigh, and plunged it into the king’s belly.
NLT.22: The dagger went so deep that the handle disappeared beneath the king’s fat. So Ehud did not pull out the dagger, and the king’s bowels emptied.
NLT.23: Then Ehud closed and locked the doors of the room and escaped down the latrine.
NLT.24: After Ehud was gone, the king’s servants returned and found the doors to the upstairs room locked. They thought he might be using the latrine in the room,
NLT.25: so they waited. But when the king didn’t come out after a long delay, they became concerned and got a key. And when they opened the doors, they found their master dead on the floor.
NLT.26: While the servants were waiting, Ehud escaped, passing the stone idols on his way to Seirah.
NLT.27: When he arrived in the hill country of Ephraim, Ehud sounded a call to arms. Then he led a band of Israelites down from the hills.
NLT.28: “Follow me,” he said, “for the LORD has given you victory over Moab your enemy.” So they followed him. And the Israelites took control of the shallow crossings of the Jordan River across from Moab, preventing anyone from crossing.
NLT.29: They attacked the Moabites and killed about 10,000 of their strongest and most able-bodied warriors. Not one of them escaped.
NLT.30: So Moab was conquered by Israel that day, and there was peace in the land for eighty years.
NLT.31: After Ehud, Shamgar son of Anath rescued Israel. He once killed 600 Philistines with an ox goad.

NIV.30: That day Moab was made subject to Israel, and the land had peace for eighty years.
NIV.31:
Shamgar
After Ehud came Shamgar son of Anath, who struck down six hundred Philistines with an oxgoad. He too saved Israel.

MSG.1: These are the nations that God left there, using them to test the Israelites who had no experience in the Canaanite wars.
MSG.2: He did it to train the descendants of Israel, the ones who had no battle experience, in the art of war.
MSG.3: He left the five Philistine tyrants, all the Canaanites, the Sidonians, and the Hivites living on Mount Lebanon from Mount Baal Hermon to Hamath's Pass.
MSG.4: They were there to test Israel and see whether they would obey God's commands that were given to their parents through Moses.
MSG.5: But the People of Israel made themselves at home among the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
MSG.6: They married their daughters and gave their own daughters to their sons in marriage. And they worshiped their gods.
MSG.7: The People of Israel did evil in God's sight. They forgot their God and worshiped the Baal gods and Asherah goddesses.
MSG.8: God's hot anger blazed against Israel. He sold them off to Cushan-Rishathaim king of Aram Naharaim. The People of Israel were in servitude to Cushan-Rishathaim for eight years.
MSG.9: The People of Israel cried out to God and God raised up a savior who rescued them: Caleb's nephew Othniel, son of his younger brother Kenaz. The Spirit of God came on him and he rallied Israel. He went out to war and God gave him Cushan-Rishathaim king of Aram Naharaim. Othniel made short work of him.
MSG.11: The land was quiet for forty years. Then Othniel son of Kenaz died.
MSG.12: But the People of Israel went back to doing evil in God's sight. So God made Eglon king of Moab a power against Israel because they did evil in God's sight.
MSG.13: He recruited the Ammonites and Amalekites and went out and struck Israel. They took the City of Palms.
MSG.14: The People of Israel were in servitude to Eglon fourteen years.
MSG.15: The People of Israel cried out to God and God raised up for them a savior, Ehud son of Gera, a Benjaminite. He was left-handed. The People of Israel sent tribute by him to Eglon king of Moab.
MSG.16: Ehud made himself a short two-edged sword and strapped it on his right thigh under his clothes.
MSG.17: He presented the tribute to Eglon king of Moab. Eglon was grossly fat.
MSG.18: After Ehud finished presenting the tribute, he went a little way with the men who had carried it.
MSG.19:
But when he got as far as the stone images near Gilgal, he went back and said, "I have a private message for you, O king."
The king told his servants, "Leave." They all left.
MSG.20: Ehud approached him—the king was now quite alone in his cool rooftop room—and said, "I have a word of God for you." Eglon stood up from his throne.
MSG.21: Ehud reached with his left hand and took his sword from his right thigh and plunged it into the king's big belly.
MSG.22: Not only the blade but the hilt went in. The fat closed in over it so he couldn't pull it out.
MSG.23: Ehud slipped out by way of the porch and shut and locked the doors of the rooftop room behind him.
MSG.24:
Then he was gone.
When the servants came, they saw with surprise that the doors to the rooftop room were locked. They said, "He's probably relieving himself in the restroom."
MSG.25: They waited. And then they worried—no one was coming out of those locked doors. Finally, they got a key and unlocked them. There was their master, fallen on the floor, dead!
MSG.26: While they were standing around wondering what to do, Ehud was long gone. He got past the stone images and escaped to Seirah.
MSG.27: When he got there, he sounded the trumpet on Mount Ephraim. The People of Israel came down from the hills and joined him. He took his place at their head.
MSG.28: He said, "Follow me, for God has given your enemies—yes, Moab!—to you." They went down after him and secured the fords of the Jordan against the Moabites. They let no one cross over.
MSG.29: At that time, they struck down about ten companies of Moabites, all of them well-fed and robust. Not one escaped.
MSG.30:
That day Moab was subdued under the hand of Israel.
The land was quiet for eighty years.
MSG.31: Shamgar son of Anath came after Ehud. Using a cattle prod, he killed six hundred Philistines single-handed. He too saved Israel.

NET.1: These were the nations the LORD permitted to remain so he could use them to test Israel — he wanted to test all those who had not experienced battle against the Canaanites.
NET.2: He left those nations simply because he wanted to teach the subsequent generations of Israelites, who had not experienced the earlier battles, how to conduct holy war.
NET.3: These were the nations: the five lords of the Philistines, all the Canaanites, the Sidonians, and the Hivites living in Mount Lebanon, from Mount Baal Hermon to Lebo-Hamath.
NET.4: They were left to test Israel, so the LORD would know if his people would obey the commands he gave their ancestors through Moses.
NET.5: The Israelites lived among the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
NET.6: They took the Canaanites’ daughters as wives and gave their daughters to the Canaanites; they worshiped their gods as well.
NET.7: The Israelites did evil in the LORD’s sight. They forgot the LORD their God and worshiped the Baals and the Asherahs.
NET.8: The LORD was furious with Israel and turned them over to King Cushan-Rishathaim of Aram-Naharaim. They were Cushan-Rishathaim’s subjects for eight years.
NET.9: When the Israelites cried out for help to the LORD, he raised up a deliverer for the Israelites who rescued them. His name was Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb’s younger brother.
NET.10: The LORD’s spirit empowered him and he led Israel. When he went to do battle, the LORD handed over to him King Cushan-Rishathaim of Aram and he overpowered him.
NET.11: The land had rest for forty years; then Othniel son of Kenaz died.
NET.12: The Israelites again did evil in the LORD’s sight. The LORD gave King Eglon of Moab control over Israel because they had done evil in the LORD’s sight.
NET.13: Eglon formed alliances with the Ammonites and Amalekites. He came and defeated Israel, and they seized the City of Date Palm Trees.
NET.14: The Israelites were subject to King Eglon of Moab for eighteen years.
NET.15: When the Israelites cried out for help to the LORD, he raised up a deliverer for them. His name was Ehud son of Gera the Benjaminite, a left-handed man. The Israelites sent him to King Eglon of Moab with their tribute payment.
NET.16: Ehud made himself a sword — it had two edges and was eighteen inches long. He strapped it under his coat on his right thigh.
NET.17: He brought the tribute payment to King Eglon of Moab. (Now Eglon was a very fat man.)
NET.18: After Ehud brought the tribute payment, he dismissed the people who had carried it.
NET.19: But he went back once he reached the carved images at Gilgal. He said to Eglon, “I have a secret message for you, O king.” Eglon said, “Be quiet!” All his attendants left.
NET.20: When Ehud approached him, he was sitting in his well-ventilated upper room all by himself. Ehud said, “I have a message from God for you.” When Eglon rose up from his seat,
NET.21: Ehud reached with his left hand, pulled the sword from his right thigh, and drove it into Eglon’s belly.
NET.22: The handle went in after the blade, and the fat closed around the blade, for Ehud did not pull the sword out of his belly.
NET.23: As Ehud went out into the vestibule, he closed the doors of the upper room behind him and locked them.
NET.24: When Ehud had left, Eglon’s servants came and saw the locked doors of the upper room. They said, “He must be relieving himself in the well-ventilated inner room.”
NET.25: They waited so long they were embarrassed, but he still did not open the doors of the upper room. Finally they took the key and opened the doors. Right before their eyes was their master, sprawled out dead on the floor!
NET.26: Now Ehud had escaped while they were delaying. When he passed the carved images, he escaped to Seirah.
NET.27: When he reached Seirah, he blew a trumpet in the Ephraimite hill country. The Israelites went down with him from the hill country, with Ehud in the lead.
NET.28: He said to them, “Follow me, for the LORD is about to defeat your enemies, the Moabites!” They followed him, captured the fords of the Jordan River opposite Moab, and did not let anyone cross.
NET.29: That day they killed about ten thousand Moabites — all strong, capable warriors; not one escaped.
NET.30: Israel humiliated Moab that day, and the land had rest for eighty years.
NET.31: After Ehud came Shamgar son of Anath; he killed six hundred Philistines with an oxgoad and, like Ehud, delivered Israel.
